Port changes the budgets follow from:

## Port changes

The first change removes instructions and keeps every barrier on a path that still touches shared data; the emulator checks qualify it.

1. **Core index and current task in `TPIDRRO_EL0`.** Bits [47:0] hold the
   current TCB address, bits [55:48] the core index, and bit 56 is set when
   the task runs at EL1. The register is UNKNOWN at reset, so each core's entry
   code writes `core << 48 | 1 << 56` beside `msr tpidr_el1`, before the first
   kernel call: `platform/a733-smp-cached/continue.S`,
   `platform/a733/cpu_continue.S` for the `a733-smp` image, and
   `platform/qemu-smp/start.S`. The context-restore path writes all three
   fields for the task it resumes. `prvSelectHighestPriorityTask`, the only
   writer of `pxCurrentTCBs[core]` once the scheduler runs, also writes the TCB
   field on its own core.
   - `ucPortGetCoreID` stays an out-of-line function; its body becomes `MRS`,
     `UBFX`, `RET`, replacing `SVC 109`.
   - `xTaskGetCurrentTaskHandle`, which `tasks.c` calls for every use of
     `pxCurrentTCB`, returns the TCB field with one `MRS` when the field is
     non-zero. A task's own TCB does not change when it migrates, so the read
     needs no mask. While the field is still zero, before the core has
     resumed a task, the function keeps the masked array read.
   - An EL0 task can read the register; it holds that task's own handle and
     core, which the API already returns.
2. **EL1 tasks mask directly.** `portDISABLE_INTERRUPTS`,
   `portENABLE_INTERRUPTS`, `uxPortSetInterruptMask` and
   `vPortClearInterruptMask` test bit 56 and, when it is set, run in line the
   PMR write and barriers of `SVC 107`, `108`, `110`, `111` and `112`. The
   inline sequence never writes `DAIF`, so the caller's `DAIF.I` is kept, as
   the SVC path keeps it by returning the caller's `SPSR`. Pre-scheduler code
   runs with `DAIF` = 0x3c0 and an ISR runs with `I` set; the upstream FromISR
   bracket, which ends with `MSR DAIFCLR, #2`, would unmask both. EL0 tasks
   keep the SVCs. An EL0 task that reaches the EL1 sequence traps on
   `MSR ICC_PMR_EL1` into the existing fault path.
3. **SGI handler without a critical section.** `FreeRTOS_SGI_Handler` only sets
   this core's yield flag, with `DAIF.I` still set from exception entry; no
   other core writes the flag. Its PMR mask pair and ISR lock go;
   `vTaskSwitchContext` still takes both locks at IRQ exit.
4. **One mask in the tick handler.** `portENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR` already
   masks, so the outer `portSET_INTERRUPT_MASK_FROM_ISR` pair goes.
5. **Per-core cache lines.** `ullPortTaskHasFPUContext` and `ullOwnedByCore`
   become one 64-byte-aligned structure per core, indexed with `LSL #6`. Each
   lock word and its recursion count get their own line (section 2.6).
   `ullCriticalNestings`, `ullPortInterruptNestings` and `ullPortYieldRequired`
   keep their symbols and 8-byte stride, because code outside this package
   reads or writes them by name (listed under outside changes). The cost: a
   critical-section or interrupt entry or exit that writes a nesting word
   first takes ownership of the line if another core wrote it since. QEMU does
   not model that transfer, so only the supervised board session shows it.

The second change weakens barriers and merges only after board qualification ([shared-helpers.md](../shared-helpers.md)):

6. **Acquire and release locks.** Take with `LDAXR`/`STXR`, release with
   `STLR`. Waiters loop on `WFE` and `LDAXR` after `SEVL`; the releasing store
   clears their exclusive monitors, which sets the event register. Only the
   holder touches the recursion count and only its core touches its ownership
   bits, so `prvGet64` and `prvSet64` drop `DSB SY`. The `DMB SY` after
   acquire and the `DSB SY`, `SEV` and `ISB` in release go.
7. **PMR writes without `DSB` or `DAIF` bracket.** Masking is one
   `MSR ICC_PMR_EL1`: IHI 0069G §12.1.6 makes PMR writes self-synchronizing,
   so no interrupt below the new mask is taken once the write executes.
   Unmasking is `MSR` then one `ISB`. §12.1.6 covers only masking, and the
   `ISB` makes an interrupt held pending by the old mask arrive at the unmask
   point instead of at a later instruction. The SVC handlers and FromISR
   functions drop `MSR DAIFSET` and `DAIFCLR`: taking the SVC or IRQ already
   set `PSTATE.I`, and the bracket served memory-mapped `GICC_PMR` on GICv2.
   `DSB SY` goes because the Redistributor observes PMR only when
   `ICC_CTLR_ELx.PMHE` = 1 (§12.1.6), and `continue.S` line 77 writes
   `ICC_CTLR_EL3` = 0. An implementation may make PMHE RAO/WI (§12.2.6), so
   `continue.S` reads `ICC_CTLR_EL3` back and faults if bit 6 is set.
   `Interrupt_Routing_Mode` 0 in every `GICD_IROUTER` write of
   `platform/a733-smp-cached/irq_table.c` stays as a second guard.

All seven edit `freertos-smp-c.patch`, `freertos-smp-asm.patch` and `freertos-smp-macro.patch`; `freertos-a733-smp.patch` still applies by offset.

conclusion:
Budgets met: EL1 critical sections issue no SVC; current-task read 0 SVC/DSB/ISB; notification 0 SVC; SGI0 handler 0 SVC, DSB, ISB and locks; cross-core round trip 58% below base against a 30% target; one patched kernel set; CMake lines 200 against 200; port cache lines per lock and per core. Budgets missed: EL1 pair 296 against 100 and same-core switch 1,320 against 800 (the design attributes both to the four vPortRecursiveLock calls, about 170 of the 296, which keep their assertions and barriers until the second change); EL0 pair 368 against 180 (it keeps two supervisor calls and the same four lock calls); tick on core 0 keeps 7 SVC and 32 DSB against targets 0 and 18 (the seven calls are SVC 117 in vInterruptCore: the tick interrupts EL0 tasks whose bit 56 is clear; an in-line SGI send from interrupt context would remove them and needs its own design); the design counted the tick baseline of 2 SVC and 21 DSB by reading source, while the measured base is 12 and 36, and the measured tree is below the measured base on both. Second-change budgets (zero DSB per pair, vTaskSwitchContext 0 DSB) were not attempted.

Consolidation: see record smp-heterogeneous-consolidation-bytes. Other findings: removing the tick handler outer mask (design item 4) makes the inner uxPortSetInterruptMaskFromISR run its DAIF bracket and PMR write, so vTaskEnterCriticalFromISR rises from 6 to 7 DSB and from 1 to 3 ISB per call while the tick as a whole falls by 4 DSB and 8 ISB. Port and kernel code grows by 472 bytes (from the inline EL1 mask sequences and TPIDRRO_EL0 fast paths; prvAddCurrentTaskToDelayedList accounts for 204 bytes); .bss grows by 496 bytes because each core FPU flag and ownership bits, and each lock, get their own 64-byte line.
narrative:
Implementation differences from the design as first written: (1) the entry code clears TPIDRRO_EL0 instead of writing the core index and bit 56; while the TCB field is zero ucPortGetCoreID also takes the supervisor call, so QEMU, the instruction models and every check that starts an image part-way keep working without an entry write. (2) The eight-core diagnostic clears the register in a733_smp_pre_scheduler instead of in platform/a733/cpu_continue.S; platform/qemu-smp/start.S and checks/cached-device-reservations.S need no change; the only edit outside the package is the storage-maintenance pin of the cached continue.S hash.

Measurement-doc findings text: - **Budgets not met with a reason in the design.** The design attributes the
  296-instruction EL1 pair and the 1,320-instruction switch to the four
  `vPortRecursiveLock` calls, which keep their assertions and barriers until
  the second change.
- **Budgets not met without a reason in the design.** The EL0 pair retires
  368 instructions against a target of 180. The tick keeps 7 `SVC` and 32
  `DSB` against targets of 0 and 18. [smp.md](../smp.md) explains both: the
  EL0 pair keeps two supervisor calls and the four lock calls, and the seven
  tick calls are `SVC 117`, which `vInterruptCore` takes because the tick
  interrupts EL0 tasks whose bit 56 is clear. The design document does not
  carry either explanation. The design's tick baseline of 2 `SVC` and 21 `DSB`
  was counted by reading the source; the measured base is 12 and 36, and the
  measured tree is below the measured base on both.
- **Barriers move from the tick into the ISR critical section.** Removing the
  tick handler's outer mask (design item 4) means the inner
  `uxPortSetInterruptMaskFromISR` no longer finds the mask already set, so it
  runs its `DAIF` bracket and PMR write. `vTaskEnterCriticalFromISR` rises
  from 6 to 7 `DSB` and from 1 to 3 `ISB` per call, while the tick as a whole
  falls by 4 `DSB` and 8 `ISB`.
- **Consolidation bytes.** In the observe and supervised images, every
  differing byte outside the build identity lies in the `configASSERT` file
  names of the kernel copy (`build/freertos-a733-smp-observe/port.c` becomes
  `build/freertos-a733-smp-cached/port.c`) and in the address immediates that
  point at those strings. After masking immediates, the disassembly of both
  images is identical to the previous build. Image sizes are unchanged, and
  the supervised `.rodata` is 8 bytes smaller. The commit message and
  [smp.md](../smp.md) state that only the 32 build-identity bytes differ; that
  holds for the cached diagnostic only.
- **Code and data size.** Port and kernel code grows by 472 bytes, from the
  inline EL1 mask sequences and the `TPIDRRO_EL0` fast paths that design items
  1 and 2 add; `prvAddCurrentTaskToDelayedList` accounts for 204 bytes.
  `.bss` grows by 496 bytes because each core's FPU flag and ownership bits,
  and each lock, get their own 64-byte line (design item 5).
